_comment: Adds an expiry rule for the reservoir build's staging prefix on edullm-landing.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Landing's expiry is PREFIX-SCOPED, not bucket-wide. As deployed on
2026-07-31 the rules cover pretrain/ curriculum/ sft/ eval/ probe/ vendor/ and _pending/ —
one per dataset family, plus the pending prefix. The reservoir build stages ~2.5 TB of
upstream documents under _ingest/, which matches NONE of them, so that data would persist
indefinitely: ~$59/month, forever, for a working set whose whole purpose ends when the
corpus is published. `ingest_reservoir.py` refuses to start until a rule covers its
destination, so deploying this is a precondition for a full run rather than a cleanup task.
WHY 30 DAYS AND NOT 14. Every existing rule is 14 days, matching the airlock's documented
scratch window. This one is longer on purpose: 14 days is the window for a PUBLISH, which is
hours of work, whereas _ingest/ holds the input to a multi-stage build whose MinHash
connected-components stage alone runs 1-2 days on-demand (§5.7), with dedup and
decontamination ahead of it. A 14-day clock could expire the corpus mid-build, and the
failure would be a partially-vanished input rather than a clean error. 30 days covers the
documented build with margin and still guarantees the bytes leave.
HOW TO DEPLOY. Lifecycle configuration is WHOLE-BUCKET: PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration
REPLACES every rule. Do not apply this file alone — it would delete the seven existing
expiry rules and the multipart-abort rule. Read the live config, append this rule, and put
the union:
aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket edullm-landing > /tmp/live.json
# merge Rules[] from this file into /tmp/live.json, then:
aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket edullm-landing \
--lifecycle-configuration file:///tmp/merged.json
Then verify the union survived, not just that the put returned 200:
aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket edullm-landing \
--query 'Rules[].ID' --output text   # expect 9 IDs, not 1
This requires the infra-deployer role; the intern session cannot and should not do it.
